text:
Hiro: quick payroll/benefits question for the international hire i'm sponsoring — start date 2024-11-05, US payroll add on 11/18. two things: 1) our hiring manager is asking if the company 401(k) match will be prorated for the first partial month since start is mid-November, and 2) the employee asked about doing a Roth conversion of old pre-tax funds into Roth IRAs after hire; any company-level blocking?

Nina (People Ops): welcome Qs. short answers: 1) match proration depends on eligibility date and payroll timing; 2) Roth conversion personal choice but watch plan rules & tax implications. details follow.

Nina (People Ops): Match proration: our policy is match is based on pay periods in which the employee is eligible and enrolled. If the employee's benefit eligibility date is 11/05 and payroll on 11/18 covers earnings through 11/17, payroll will withhold and the match will apply for that pay period. We do not do calendar-month pro-rating independent of payroll runs. So if the employee is active and enrolled in 401(k) before the payroll cutoff, they'll receive match for that paycheck (even if it's a partial-month hire).

Sanjay - Benefits: adding: two caveats: (a) some match programs have a vesting schedule that starts on the hire date; prorated match counts toward vesting but vesting still follows the schedule. (b) If you put a plan-level waiting period (we sometimes delay match for the first 30 days for contractors), that could block initial match. For typical FT hires, no waiting period.

Hiro: got it. manager will enroll them immediately. second Q re: Roth conversion 1: can they convert old pre-tax funds from a previous employer plan into a Roth IRA after they join? will our payroll/plan block any external rollovers/conversions?

Sanjay - Benefits: conversions of outside rollover funds are handled by the receiving custodian (Roth IRA provider) and the former employer plan; that's not something Payroll or our 401(k) recordkeeper blocks. Two notes: (1) if they want an in-plan Roth conversion (pre-tax money inside our plan -> Roth within the same plan), that's subject to our plan document and may not be allowed; check Plan Section 5.4. (2) taxable event: conversion of pre-tax to Roth triggers income tax in the conversion year. Recommend they consult a tax advisor.

Payroll Bot: FYI: Payroll cannot execute Roth IRA conversions. We can facilitate rollovers to the new plan's trustee if the plan allows inbound rollover, but taxes and Roth conversions are client/individual actions outside payroll.

Hiro: do we have any additional paperwork the new hire should complete to allow a rollover (e.g., allowing inbound rollover from prior 401k) or is that handled post-hire directly with the trustee?

Nina (People Ops): inbound rollover permissions: they should check the new plan's participant portal after account setup. We allow incoming rollovers; the employee signs rollover paperwork in the recordkeeper portal. For timing, suggest waiting until their new 401(k) account is provisioned (usually 1-2 payrolls after hire) before initiating a rollover to avoid reconciliation headaches.

Sanjay - Benefits: Action items for manager/Hiro: (1) enroll employee in 401(k) ASAP in Workday before the 11/18 payroll cutoff, (2) employee should set deferral % and tick the "allow incoming rollover" option if offered, (3) if considering an in-plan Roth conversion, DM me so I can confirm plan permissions.

Hiro: perfect. i'll tell the manager to enroll them today and i'll loop in the candidate on rollover timing. thanks! :relaxed:

Nina (People Ops): ping this thread if payroll cutoff time is tight and we can confirm with Jorge in Payroll.

Payroll Bot: Cutoff reminder: for 11/18 pay, final changes must be submitted by 11/13 5pm PT.
